title: Phosphate → fertilizer → food chain

chokepoint.physics: ~70% of reserves are in Morocco; no substitute for phosphorus

h1: For food, the mine is the chokepoint
deck: Most of the value chains in this atlas find the bottleneck downstream of the mine. Phosphorus is the exception: it has no substitute in agriculture, its only real source is phosphate rock, and about 70% of the world's reserves sit in a single country. Here the raw resource is the binding constraint.
byline: reserves ≠ production ≠ fertilizer ≠ food — but for phosphorus there is no plan B
correction: The atlas's usual finding — 'the refiner is not the source' — inverts for phosphorus. There is no synthetic substitute for it and no alternative resource to phosphate rock, so the reserve base itself is the chokepoint, and it is extraordinarily concentrated.

history.title: Phosphate-rock mine production shifted to China, 2000–2024
history.note: BGS/USGS (mine production %), from the atlas's own data. The US fell from ~21% to ~8%; China rose from ~14% to ~44% (peaking near 52% in 2015); Morocco stayed ~14-18%. Note the twist: current output moved to China, but the long-run RESERVE base (~70%) stayed in Morocco — production and reserves point to different countries.

sections.h2: 1 · Reserves are even more concentrated than production

panels.note: USGS. Morocco (incl. Western Sahara) holds ~50 billion t — about 70% of world reserves. Reserves are the long-run ceiling; they are far more concentrated than current output.

panels.h3: Production is more spread — for now
panels.text: China is currently the largest producer of phosphate rock, ahead of Morocco, the United States and Russia. But several producers mine from limited reserves and restrict exports to protect domestic fertilizer supply; over the long run, output gravitates toward where the rock actually is.
panels.flag: reserves are the ceiling, not output

sections.h2: 2 · The chokepoint does not move downstream — it stays at the resource

panels.text: In the tech chains, the bottleneck migrates to a furnace, a fab or a magnet. Phosphorus cannot do that: there is no synthetic substitute and no alternative ore. Morocco's OCP has also moved downstream into phosphoric acid and finished fertilizer, so it holds both the reserve base AND a large share of processing — concentration at two stages at once.
panels.flag: an inversion of the atlas thesis

panels.h3: The demand that cannot be switched off
panels.text: P₂O₅ contained in fertilizer used worldwide, rising toward ~52 Mt by 2028. Every tonne of it ultimately traces to phosphate rock; there is no recycling loop at scale to relieve it.
panels.note: USGS. Fertilizer is the overwhelming end use of phosphate rock.

sections.h2: 3 · The other two nutrients are locked up too (N-P-K)

panels.h3: Each fertilizer nutrient has its own concentration

cards.d: Phosphate rock, ~70% of reserves in Morocco. No substitute. The subject of this chain.
Potash, dominated by Canada, Russia and Belarus. Russia + Belarus supply was disrupted after 2022 sanctions.
Fixed from the air by Haber-Bosch, but powered by natural gas — so nitrogen fertilizer tracks the price and security of gas.

panels.h3: The long-run risk is different from a chokepoint
panels.text: Phosphorus is not scarce this decade, but it is finite, non-substitutable and lost to runoff rather than recycled — so the security question is less 'who can cut supply tomorrow' and more 'who owns the only resource, and how efficiently is it used'. Recovery from wastewater and manure exists but is nowhere near the scale of demand.
panels.flag: a resource question, not a refining one

trade_intro: BACI shows the traded forms — phosphate rock, DAP/MAP fertilizer and potash — as a consistent monetary series. Export restrictions (China, Russia) and captive domestic use mean trade shares understate where the resource actually sits; read them as availability, not reserves.
